result.summary: Read lib/letflow/design/iss0721-entity-event-type-seeding.md directly (not CODE-DESIGNER's handoff summary), plus event_types.ex's and tenant_provisioning.ex's actual bodies. 5 of 6 gate checks pass; 1 BLOCKER: section 5 embeds a real, copy-pasteable Elixir `with`-chain as the fix's 'New' code, which is an implementation-code body, not a signature/shape -- and this project's own cited precedent (iss072-event-type-registration.md section 2.1, which THIS design lists in its own section 0 'Sources read') deliberately avoided exactly this by describing the control-flow change in prose ('described here as the required control-flow shape, not as code; ELIXIR-DEV chooses the exact construct'). Section 2's `@spec` block is fine (spec, not a body) and its two clauses are described in prose, matching the precedent's style -- section 5 is the sole violation, but it is decisive under check (4)'s 'no .ex implementation code bodies -- signatures and type shapes only' with no partial credit. Independently verified findings on the other checks: (1) PASS -- every element of ISSUE-FIXER's step-01 'WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE' (new function, call-site line ~390, exact schema_name argument, ok/error normalization) traces to a concrete design section (2, 3, 4, 5 respectively), cited by section number in the design's own section 0. (2) PASS -- idempotency claim independently re-verified against event_types.ex:117-140's actual body (not copied from the design's own assertion): the `Enum.reduce_while/3` in `seed!/1` does catch `{:error, :duplicate_event_type_version}` per event-type and folds it into `skipped` while still returning `{:ok, seed_result()}` -- matches section 4's claim exactly. (3) FAIL, see above -- section 5's 'New' with-chain block. (5) PASS, and independently resolved rather than just checked for presence: I read replay_migrations/2's actual `@spec` (tenant_provisioning.ex:364-371) myself -- it lists only `{:error, :tenant_not_provisioned}` and `{:error, {:migration_failed, Exception.t()}}`, NOT `{:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, term()}}`, even though the sibling `maybe_seed_platform_event_types/2` call already wired into the with-chain today already produces that exact error shape. So the design's speculative framing in section 7 ('it should, if ISS-0072's own fix updated it identically') is answered, and answered in the direction the design did not assume: the @spec does NOT already cover it, so ELIXIR-DEV needs a concrete one-line @spec addition, not just a 'check and see.' The design's own text already tells ELIXIR-DEV to add it if missing (mechanical, not a design decision), which is enough to satisfy this run's acceptance criterion 5 on its own terms ('resolved or explicitly left as a mechanical note ... not silently dropped') -- flagging this only so CODE-DESIGNER can tighten section 7's wording to state the confirmed fact instead of the open conditional, while reworking the section 5 BLOCKER. (4/no-TBD) PASS -- no deferral/TBD language found via read-through; the one open item (spec coverage) is explicitly named, not silently dropped. (6) PASS -- section 6's regression-test spec is concrete and actionable: real provisioning path with no manual seed!/1 call, a real entity-record write asserted to succeed (not just Registry.get_type/2), an explicit fail-on-pre-fix-code requirement naming the exact {:error, :unknown_event_type} reproduction, and a second-call idempotency assertion -- satisfies WF-03's fail-then-pass rule.

issues.description: lib/letflow/design/iss0721-entity-event-type-seeding.md section 5's 'New' code fence (lines ~123-128) is a real, directly-pasteable Elixir with-chain -- implementation code, not a signature/shape, in violation of this gate's check 4. Rework: replace the fenced 'New' code block with a prose description of the required control-flow shape (a second `:ok <-` clause added to the existing with-chain, calling maybe_seed_entity_event_types/2 with the same using_default_manifest? gate and schema_name), mirroring this design's own cited precedent lib/letflow/design/iss072-event-type-registration.md section 2.1, which states the equivalent change as prose explicitly labelled 'described here as the required control-flow shape, not as code; ELIXIR-DEV chooses the exact construct.' The 'Current' code fence quoting the existing, already-shipped with-chain for context is not itself a problem and may stay.

Section 7's open question is phrased as an unresolved conditional ('it should, if ISS-0072's own fix updated it identically') when the actual answer is directly checkable and, checked here, is 'no': replay_migrations/2's @spec (tenant_provisioning.ex:364-371) does not list {:error, {:event_type_seed_failed, term()}} today. Not a BLOCKER on its own (this run's acceptance criterion 5 permits leaving this as an explicit mechanical note), but tighten the wording while reworking the section 5 BLOCKER so ELIXIR-DEV is told the fact, not sent to go check it.
